# Methodological payoff

The framework changes constructive-QFT proof design in four concrete ways.

1. **Theorem interfaces become explicit.** Each representation change names
   its physical observable domain and every prerequisite of the desired
   inference.
2. **Failed bounds are localized.** A failed uniform conditional estimate can
   be distinguished from a failed gauge quotient, a missing normalization,
   or an incomplete observable core.
3. **Recovery determines state design.** If coarse graining forgets boundary
   charge or history, the retained state must be enlarged until the missing
   quantity is either manifest or theorem-recoverable.
4. **Limits become part of the property.** A positive finite-volume number is
   not the same predicate as a uniform positive physical rate.

The result is prescriptive: it tells the researcher which theorem to attempt
next and which apparent shortcut cannot establish the target property.
